source.title: ‘We are still here’: Tribes reclaiming out-of-state ancestral homelands
source.author: Nancy Marie Spears
source.annotation: May 23, 2022 Native-authored reporting, with original interviews concerning Arbeka's Oxford homeland. Read the opening Muscogee discussion and closing Galen Cloud quotation; other sections concern different nations. Distinct from the Mvskoke Media festival report. This is reporting with attributed voices, not a tribal policy document or evidence of a completed property transfer.

proposedSectionReplacement.targetTitle: Returning to the homeland and shaping public history
proposedSectionReplacement.text: The inaugural Reyicepes festival in Oxford brought Muscogee citizens, leaders, artists and local residents together in 2022. Mvskoke Media reports ancestral-trail walks, cultural activities and educational partnerships. Separate reporting by Nancy Marie Spears adds original interviews: preservation manager RaeLynn A. Butler identifies the pre-removal Arbeka site and work by city and tribal officials to protect nearby lands. National Council representative Galen Cloud contrasts his journey to Alabama with his ancestors’ forced journey west, emphasizes the importance of present visibility, and describes the continued importance of the fire carried from the homeland. These are specific, attributed interpretations of return and preservation. They do not establish a completed land transfer, title ownership or a single view held by every Arbeka person.

integrationNotes: Remove p2-yardeka from the strict minimum and remove or separately label the civic-service paragraph supported only by that regional report. Retain the Sten Joddi family reconnection account with its individual scope clear.

The new report was read in full. Its substantive Arbeka material is the opening discussion, the Oxford photograph caption and the closing Cloud quotation. Do not transfer facts about Kaw, Osage, Shawnee or Wyandotte land projects to Arbeka.

Native-authored classification is supported by the publisher's author page, which identifies Spears as a Cherokee Nation member: https://sourcenm.com/author/nancymariespears/ . Gaylord News is a university reporting project and Source New Mexico is part of States Newsroom; no claim of tribal ownership of the publisher is intended.

Cloud is identified as a National Council representative; Butler is identified as the Nation's preservation manager. Neither is described here as an Arbeka hereditary officer. The report is primary evidence for their dated interview statements, not a primary land deed or removal-era record.

The marker and the 2023 report's Jim Fife/Dorsey Fife discussion independently support a public ancestral connection. The report remains an archival synthesis pending inspection of the original affidavit. No other material factual issue was found in the Abihka draft audit.
